entries.german:
1369. 2. Februar. 0. A0. — Marquard von Mö'dling und seine Hausfrau Zdenka verkaufen dem Abt und dem Convent des Klosters zu Hohenfurt das Dorf Su chenthal sammt allem Zubehör um 61 Schock und 41 grosse Prager Pfenninge und einen Passauer Pfenning. 1369. 18. März. Krumau. — Jodok und Johann Gebrüder von Rosenberg als Vormünder der Waisen nach Ludwig von Xwidlern schlichten den zwischen diesem einerseits und dem Abte Heinrich und dem Convente zu Hohenfurt andererseits wegen des Zehnten vom Hofe im Dorfe Michnüz obschwcbenden Streit.

Ich Marchwart von Metling vnd ich Sdenka sein hawsvrawe vnd alle venser paider gerben veriehen vnd tun chunt offenbar mit dem gegenwortigem prief allen lewten, di in sehent lesent oder hoerent lesen, di nu lebent oder hernach chvemftig sein, daz wir mit guetem willen mit veraintem rat mit verdachtem mvet vnd mit wizzen vnd gunst aller venserr vrewnt vnverschaidenleichen vnbe- twungenleichen mit gesuntem leib zu den zeiten, do wir iz wol tuen mochten, den erbern vnd den geistlichen hern dem abpt conuent vnd sammvng dez chlosters ze Hohenfurt haben verchaufft recht vnd redleichen ewigleichen in dem dorf, daz mit namen gehaissen ist Czuchadol vnd gelegen pey dem dorff, daz do haisset Ainsidel, mit allen nveczen mit allen rechten mit allen sachen mit wazzer mit pechen zu holcz vnd zu veld versuecht vnd vnversucht mit visch- waid mit wiezzmait vnd mit allen andern dingen, sam aigens recht ist vnd sam wir iz in nvcz vnd gewer haben von venserm vater vnd von venserm vater vnd von vensern vorvadern ingehabt an allew an sprach vnd an allen krieg, daz venser rechtes vreys erb vnd a igen gewesen ist vnversprochens vnd vnverchummerts, vmb ains vnd sechszig schok grozzer phenning Prager mvencz vnd vmb ain vnd vierzig grozz vnd vmb ein Pazzawer phenning, der wir aller schon gancz vnd gar von in mit beraiten phenning gewert vnd gericht sein zu rechter zeit vnd zu rechten tegen vor erbern pidern lewten. Wir verhaizzen in auch vuer allez abschvetten vnd vuer abzuloezen von vens vnd von allen vensern vrewnten vnd vuer allen zuchvemf- tigen chrieg vnd schaden, der ¡n mit einem landes recht auf)' daz selb erb vnd aigen zins oder gelts zu chvemftigleichen get oder wiert von chainerlay menschen, daz wir in den gancz vnd gar zu aller zeit an aller stat schvellen auz richten vnd richtig machen mit venserm aigenheftigem guet vnd mit venser aigen zervng an alle ir mvehe vnd an allen iern schaden. Dar veber zu einer pezzer Siche rung hab wir in geben vnd geseczt di erbern lewt, di sich durch vensern willen noch venser pet mit iern trewen vnd mit ieren an- hangunden insigeln in dem prieff verhaizzen vnd verpinten, daz si mit sampt vens sein ¡er recht ausrichtet* noch dez landes recht ze Pehem, di her nach sich mit namen in dem prief offenleichen er kennen. Dar veber ich Mikscho von Malating vnd ich Dwuersat von Cypping vnd ich Troyan von Tewdlieb all drei besunderleichen ver- piuten vens an disem prieff mit vensern trewen vnd mit vensern an- hangunden insigeln mit gesampter hant an allez gever zu dem obgenanten Marchwarten von Metling noch seiner pet willen vnd aller seiner gerben, daz wir sein vnd schvellen sein rechtew vnd gancz trew ausrichter an aller stat zu aller zeit noch landes recht ze Pehem mit venser aigen zerung vnd aigenheftigem gvet vmb alle sach gelveb red vnd chauff, sam hie vor an dem prief verhaizzen Tnd geschriben stet, den erbern geistleichen hern dem abpt vnd dem conuent dez chlosters ze Hohenfurt, also daz in an den sachen nichtes schol abpgen an vens weder mit red noch an werchen. Ge- schech dez nicht, welhew zwen man vnter vens viern mit namen vadert vnd haist, di schvellen an alle widerred ein iedleicher mit einem knecht vnd mit zwain pherchten laisten vnd einvaren in eines erberigen gastgeben havz in der stat ze Cbrumpnawe oder ze Rosen- berch, wo man im hin zaiget, vnd schvellen von dann nicht auzchoe- men, venczen dem obgenanten chloster werd richtig gemacht aller chrieg vnd alle sach. Daz alle sach chauff red gelveb diez prieffs stet gancz vnzuprochen ewigleichen bleib, dar vmb geh ich vorge nanter Marchwart von Metling mit den egenanten erbern lewten, Füiit..,.. Л brlí. II. Bd. XXIII. IQ 146 di diser sach vnd chauff vnd prieff auzrichter sein mit sampt mir, disen prieff dem oft genantenten (sic) chloster vnd sammvng ze Hohenfurt zu einem ewigen offen sichtigen verehvend versigelten mit meinem aigen anhanguuden insigel. Diser prieff ist gegeben do noch Christes gepuert ergangen waren drewczehen hvndert jar, do noch in dem newn vnd sechszigstem jar an vensirr vrawen tag zu der lyechtmess. Es ist nur mehr das an einem Pergamentstreifen bangende, und ¡n weissem Wachs abgedruckte Siegel des Urkundenausstellers vorhanden. Vcrgl. CXII. d. cxxx. 1369. 18. März. Krumau. — Jodok und Johann Gebrüder von Rosenberg als Vormünder der Waisen nach Ludwig von Xwidlern schlichten den zwischen diesem einerseits und dem Abte Heinrich und dem Convente zu Hohenfurt andererseits wegen des Zehnten vom Hofe im Dorfe Michnüz obschwcbenden Streit. Cunctos humanitatis actus, ne in obliuionis materiam delabantur, sapientum consueuit discrecio litterarum testimonio roborare. Sed quia inter honorabiles el religiosos viros dominum Henricum abbatem totumque conuentum monasteríi in Alionado ab vna et . . orphanos quondam domini Ludwici de Czwetlaren super decimis de curia ara- ture in Michnicz villa per ipsos orphanos dicto abbati suoque con- uentui assignandis lis et contencio parte ab altera vertebatur, nos vero Jodocus et Johannes de Rosenberg fratres tutores et fidei com- missarii orpbanorum predictorum nomine tutorio arbitrando pronun- tiantes mandamus, quatenus memorati orphani aut legittimus prefate curie in Michnicz possessor, dum et quando annonas ab antiquo dare consuetas cuiuslibet generis preter aut omnes insimul messuerint effectualiter in ipsa curia per vnum discretum nuntium cum sufficient testimonio domestico, aut magistro curie in Hodonicz huiusmodi messem sic iam ad plenum factam sub ypoteca et ammissione duorum talentorum denariorum Wyennensium debeant declarare; quod si non fecerint, tune ipsos mox preallegato monasterio in duobus talentis denariorum memoratorum nomine vadii fore arbitramur debitorie obligatos, vt veniente magistro curie in Hodonicz prius dicte et sic presente in sepefata curia Michnicz annonarum decime debito et consueto intersigno consignentur et sic consignate per ipsum curie Michnicz prouisorem ad ipsam conduete in vno singulari et specia- 147 liter loco deputato vsque ad extrituracionem debent irrefragabiliter reseruare, etrituratas vero annonas prenarratus abbas aut suns con- uentus propriis suis sumptibus in prelibata curia Michnicz ipsas decimas recipere debet tofaliter et in toto solum ibidem stramiua immota dimitiendo. Sin autem . . magister curie Hodonicz prius fate ad consignandum decimas per intimationem nuncii, ut prefertur non veniret, extunc ipsi orphani aut ipsius curie Michnicz possessor easdem decimas deducere poterit cum ceteris suis annonis, prout ipsius discrecionis consciencia eum edocebit, difficultate qualibet non obstante. Vt autem omnia premissa in singulis suis clausulis rata grata permaneant atque firma presentes litteras scribi ipsasque sigil- lorum nostrorum appensione iussimus in fidem validiorem communiri. Datum in Chrumpnaw anno domini millesimo trecentesimo sexagesimo nono dominica, qua „Judica" decantatur. Die an Pergamentstreifen hängenden Siegel in rothem Wachs bei CXI V. beschrieben.
entries.english:
2 February 1369. Marquard von Mödling and his wife Zdenka sell to the abbot and convent of Hohenfurt Monastery the village of Suchenthal with all its appurtenances for 61 schock and 41 large Prague pennies and one Passau penny.

18 March 1369, Krumau. Jodok and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg and guardians of the orphans of Ludwig von Xwidlern, settle the dispute between the latter on one side and Abbot Heinrich and the convent of Hohenfurt on the other concerning the tithe from a farm in the village of Michnüz.

I, Marchwart von Metling, and I, Sdenka, his wife, and all our joint heirs openly declare and make known by this present letter to all people who see it, read it, or hear it read, now living or to come, that, of our own free will, with united counsel, considered intent, and the knowledge and consent of all our friends, without compulsion and in sound health at a time when we were able to do so, we have rightfully and lawfully sold forever to the honorable spiritual lords, the abbot, convent, and community of Hohenfurt Monastery, the village called Czuchadol, situated near the village called Ainsidel, with all appurtenances, rights, and possessions, with water, streams, woodland and fields, cultivated and uncultivated, with fishing and meadows, and all other things, as is right for freehold and as we have held it in use and possession from our father and forebears, without claim or dispute, as our rightful, free inheritance and freehold, unchallenged and unencumbered, for 61 schock of large Prague pennies, 41 large pennies, and one Passau penny. We have already received the entire sum from them in ready money, in full and at the proper time, before honorable, upright people.

We also promise to indemnify and protect them against every claim and to redeem them from any future dispute or loss affecting that same inheritance, freehold, rent, or payment under the law of the land, whoever may bring it. At all times and in every place we shall fully satisfy and clear them, from our own property and at our own expense, without any effort or loss to them. For further security, we have appointed and bound the honorable men who, at our request and on our behalf, promise under their faith and attached seals in this letter to ensure our lawful performance under the law of Bohemia. I, Mikscho von Malating, I, Dwuersat von Cypping, and I, Troyan von Tewdlieb, each separately bind ourselves by our faith and attached seals, jointly and without deceit, to the aforesaid Marchwart von Metling, at his request and that of all his heirs: we shall faithfully and fully perform his obligations everywhere and at all times according to the law of Bohemia, at our own expense and from our own property, concerning every matter, obligation, agreement, and purchase promised and written above to the honorable spiritual lords, the abbot and convent of Hohenfurt Monastery, so that nothing in word or deed shall be lacking to them.

If this does not happen, then whichever two of us the four named men summon shall, without objection, each go with a servant and two horses and lodge in an honorable inn in the town of Krumau or Rosenberg, wherever they are directed, and shall not leave until all disputes and matters have been made right for the aforesaid monastery. So that every matter, purchase, agreement, and obligation in this letter may remain wholly unbroken forever, I, the aforesaid Marchwart von Metling, together with the honorable men named above who are guarantors of this matter, purchase, and letter, have sealed this letter with my own seal and given it to the aforesaid monastery and community as a permanent public record. This letter was issued in the year 1369 from the birth of Christ, on Candlemas, the feast of Our Lady. Only the issuer’s seal remains, stamped in white wax and hanging from a parchment strip. Compare CXII d and CXXX.

CXXX. 18 March 1369, Krumau. Jodok and Johann, brothers von Rosenberg and guardians and trustees of the aforesaid orphans, issue an arbitral decision and order: Since a dispute had arisen between the honorable and religious Lord Heinrich, abbot, and the whole convent of the monastery at Hohenfurt on one side, and the orphans of the late Lord Ludwig von Czwetlaren on the other, concerning tithes from the ploughland farm in the village of Michnicz, which the orphans were to assign to the said abbot and convent, we, Jodocus and Hans von Rosenberg, brothers, guardians and trustees of the aforesaid orphans, acting in our capacity as guardians and arbitrating, pronounce and order as follows. Whenever the aforesaid orphans or the lawful possessor of the aforesaid farm at Michnicz have actually harvested all together or separately the grain crops customarily given from olden times, they must declare the completed harvest at that farm to one prudent messenger, with sufficient testimony from the household, or to the steward of the farm at Hodonicz, under penalty of forfeiting two talents of Viennese pennies. If they fail to do so, we judge them immediately liable to the aforesaid monastery for those two talents as a pledge. When the aforesaid steward of Hodonicz arrives at the said farm at Michnicz, the customary tithe owed in grain must be marked out in his presence; once marked, the farm’s manager must bring it to one particular and specially designated place and keep it there without fail until threshing. The aforesaid abbot or convent must collect the tithe grain there, at their own expense and in full, leaving only the straw in place. But if the steward of Hodonicz, having been notified by messenger as aforesaid, does not come to mark out the tithe, then the orphans or possessor of the farm at Michnicz may carry away those tithes with their other grain, as their conscience and judgment direct, without any hindrance.

So that all the foregoing may remain valid, approved, and firm in every clause, we have ordered these present letters to be written and strengthened by the attachment of our seals as further proof. Given at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1369, on the Sunday on which “Judica” is sung. The seals, hanging from parchment strips and made of red wax, are described at CXIV.
